# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤟]

I need to figure out what these gestures mean. Mute is sending me gesture patterns, likely trying to encode information about the manual since Mute can't speak to me directly with words that matter until I understand the code - wait, actually Mute CAN speak and I CAN hear (I'm Deaf... wait no, Deaf means I cannot hear).

Let me reconsider: I am Deaf - I cannot hear speech, only see gestures. Mute cannot speak anyway. So gestures are Mute's only way to reach me. I need to try to interpret these as some kind of code, but without prior agreement, I should report what I see on the bomb first, since Blind needs my description relayed - but I can't speak to Blind directly with useful info... actually I CAN speak, and Blind can hear me. Let me check: Deaf's channels - "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." So I can speak to Blind.

I should describe the bomb to Blind via speech, and try to signal to Mute via gesture what I see, since Mute reads the manual and needs my bomb info to cross-reference.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Display shows 0. Light is green. There is one large button labeled push to defuse. Three wires: wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "🖐"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "✌"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]

Mute is sending escalating thumbs-up counts: 1, then 2, then 3. This looks like Mute is trying to establish a numbering scheme - possibly confirming receipt of my wire info, or indicating which wire number corresponds to something in the manual (e.g., "wire 1 = safe/ok", "wire 2 = ok", "wire 3 = ok"), or counting up to establish they can send numbers via repeated gestures.

Since I already sent Blind the full bomb description, and Mute seems to be counting 1-2-3 (possibly matching my wire numbers 1,2,3), this could be Mute's way of asking me to confirm/repeat wire colors in order, or Mute might be building a code where thumbs-up count = number reference.

I should acknowledge and try to establish a clearer coding scheme. Let me try mirroring numbers with distinct symbols per wire color attribute, or just wait to see if Mute clarifies further since I can't ask questions via gesture easily (Mute can't hear/see my speech-gestures distinction - wait, Mute cannot hear my speech at all, only sees my gestures).

I'll gesture back a distinct pattern per wire to see if Mute can build correspondence, and continue relaying to Blind.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟"])
speak(to="blind", text="Still the same: display 0, light green, one large push to defuse button, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Waiting for instructions from mute relayed through me or directly to you.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]

Mute sent [✌ ✌] again - this matches the second message from Turn 1 exactly. This is likely Mute repeating a specific instruction/query about wire 2 (yellow), or confirming something with a fixed code that means "wire 2" or "yellow".

Given the pattern from Turn 1 was [☝ 🖐], [✌ ✌], [🤟 🤟] - three distinct two-symbol gestures, possibly meant to represent three items (matching my three wires: green, yellow, red). Mute repeating [✌ ✌] now suggests they want to focus on or confirm the second item specifically - which in my wire list is wire 2, yellow.

This could mean: "cut wire 2" or "wire 2 is the one mentioned in the manual" or Mute is asking me to confirm wire 2's color again.

I should respond by confirming wire 2 is yellow, and speak to Blind suggesting wire 2 might be the key wire, while being cautious since I don't have full certainty.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "✌"])
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has repeated a signal matching wire 2. Wire 2 is yellow. This may indicate wire 2 is significant per the manual, possibly the one to cut - but wait for confirmation before touching anything.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]

Mute sent [👎] followed by [✌ ✌] again. The thumbs-down likely means "no, that's not right" - perhaps rejecting my confirmation gesture from before, or indicating wire 2 is NOT the one to cut / is dangerous. Then repeating [✌ ✌] to re-emphasize wire 2 specifically.

This could mean: "No - wire 2 is bad/dangerous, do NOT cut it" or "No, you misunderstood, but yes wire 2 is what I'm referring to."

Given the thumbs-down precedes the repeat, it likely corrects my previous interpretation: Mute is saying "no" to something and then reiterating wire 2. Perhaps my gesture back of [✌✌] was interpreted as "confirm cut wire 2" and Mute is saying "no, don't cut it" while still pointing at wire 2 as the relevant one (maybe the dangerous one to avoid).

I need to relay this caution to Blind clearly.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👎"])
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signaled no, then pointed again at wire 2 which is yellow. This suggests wire 2 is dangerous - do not cut wire 2. Wait for further clarification on which wire is safe to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute sent [👎 👎] then [☝]. The double thumbs-down might be reacting to my [👎] gesture - "no, that's not what I meant" - meaning my interpretation was wrong. Then [☝] (index finger up) which in the original Turn 1 sequence appeared as the first symbol of [☝ 🖐], associated with wire 1 potentially, or simply meaning "one" / "first" / "wait".

Let me reconsider the whole sequence: Turn 1 Mute sent three two-symbol gestures: [☝🖐], [✌✌], [🤟🤟]. These could each encode a distinct concept - maybe one per wire (1, 2, 3) with the second symbol being an instruction (cut/don't cut). [☝🖐] = wire1+something, [✌✌]=wire2+wire2(?), [🤟🤟]=wire3+something.

Now Mute is reacting negatively to my gesture-mirroring attempts, and sent [☝] alone - possibly meaning "wire 1" or "first, listen". My mirroring back gestures might be confusing Mute since gestures I send aren't being distinguished from Mute's own by context, or Mute realizes I can't verify without more info.

I think my repeating gestures back isn't working. I should stop mirroring and instead just relay raw bomb facts, and let Mute try a cleaner signal. Let me acknowledge with a neutral gesture and wait for Mute's next clearer attempt.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's signals are unclear still. My previous guess about wire 2 being dangerous may be wrong - mute pushed back twice. Hold off on cutting any wire. Bomb still shows display 0, light green, button large push to defuse, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 red.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute sent [☝] twice now. This is a simple, repeated, single symbol - likely meaning "wire 1" or "look at point one" or trying to get my attention on something specific without the confusion of multi-symbol combos. Given the repetition and simplicity, I think Mute is trying to establish: "☝ = 1" as a stable reference, separate from my mirroring which seemed to cause confusion (thumbs down).

Perhaps Mute wants me to respond with information *about* wire 1, or Mute is establishing a numbering: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3 (which matches finger-counting gestures: index finger=1, peace sign=2, three fingers=3). That fits! ☝ (one finger) = 1, ✌ (two fingers) = 2, 🤟 (three fingers, sort of) = 3.

So Mute's original three gestures [☝🖐], [✌✌], [🤟🤟] likely encoded: (1, X), (2, X), (3, X) where the second symbol is some attribute per wire number from the manual. 🖐 = open hand (5?), maybe representing "safe" or a category. Then repeated ✌✌ = emphasis on wire 2. Then 👎👎 rejecting my thumbs-down back, and ☝☝ now - repeating "1" twice, perhaps meaning "wire 1, wire 1" - emphasizing wire 1 is important, or answering my last message somehow.

Given uncertainty, I should not guess further blindly. Let me respond by using the same finger-counting convention to ask Mute a direct question: which wire to cut. I'll gesture ☝ ✌ 🤟 in sequence with a query-like structure isn't possible without speech reaching Mute (Mute can't hear). I can only gesture back.

I'll try acknowledging I understand ☝=1 by gesturing back ☝, and speak to Blind to hold, noting wire 1 (green) now seems highlighted.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
speak(to="blind", text="Mute is now repeating a single signal that may correspond to wire 1 (green). Possible that wire 1 is the safe wire to cut, or the important one. Still uncertain - do not act yet. Wires remain 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red; display 0; light green; button push to defuse.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤝]

Blind sent me a gesture now too - [🤝] (handshake), likely meaning "agreement" or "understood" or "ready to proceed" or acknowledging receipt of my relayed info. This is a positive/cooperative signal.

Mute continues sending [☝] - consistent single-symbol repetition, reinforcing "1" as the key reference.

Given the consistency, I'm fairly convinced ☝ = "1" (wire 1). Mute seems to be settling on wire 1 as the answer after the back-and-forth confusion. Blind's handshake suggests readiness to act once we agree.

I should relay to Blind: "the signal indicates wire 1 (green)" and see if Blind can act, while also gesturing back to Mute a confirmation.

However, I must be careful - this is a bomb, wrong action kills everyone. Given the repeated, insistent, simple signal (☝ alone, repeated across turns without further elaboration or negation), and no thumbs-down since I stopped mirroring the double-symbol combos, I'll treat this as Mute confirming wire 1 is the one to cut.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has repeated a single signal consistently pointing to wire 1, which is green. I believe wire 1 is the wire to cut. No further correction has come from mute since I stopped my double-symbol mirroring. Proceed to cut wire 1 if you are ready and this matches what you understand.")
wait()
```
